questions.stem: Fred's data role requires him to maintain system security plans and to ensure that system users and support staff get the training they need about security practices and acceptable use. What is the role that Fred is most likely to hold in the organization?
questions.explanation: NIST SP 800-18 describes system owner responsibilities that include helping to develop system security plans, maintaining the plan, ensuring training, and identifying, implementing, and assessing security controls. A data owner is more likely to delegate these tasks to the system owner. Custodians may be asked to enforce those controls, whereas a user will be directly affected by them.
optionNotes: Incorrect. The data owner is ultimately accountable for the data and usually delegates system security plan upkeep and training tasks to the system owner. It doesn't do these hands-on duties itself.

Correct. NIST SP 800-18 makes the system owner responsible for developing and maintaining the system security plan, making sure users and support staff are trained, and identifying, implementing and assessing security controls.
Incorrect. Users are the people directly affected by the security controls and training. They don't maintain security plans or make sure others get trained.
Incorrect. Custodians do the day-to-day work of protecting data and may be asked to enforce controls. They don't own or maintain system security plans or set training requirements.

questions.stem: Sally is using IPsec's ESP component in transport mode. What important information should she be aware of about transport mode?
options: Transport mode provides full encryption of the entire IP packet.
Transport mode adds a new, unencrypted header to ensure that packets reach their destination.
Transport mode does not encrypt the header of the packet.
Transport mode provides no encryption; only tunnel mode provides encryption.
questions.explanation: ESP's Transport mode encrypts IP packet data but leaves the packet header unencrypted. Tunnel mode encrypts the entire packet and adds a new header to support transmission through the tunnel.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Encrypting the whole IP packet is what tunnel mode does. Transport mode encrypts only the payload and leaves the original header readable.
Incorrect. Adding a new outer header is a feature of tunnel mode, which wraps the whole encrypted original packet inside it. Transport mode keeps and reuses the original IP header.
Correct. In transport mode, ESP encrypts the packet's data (payload) but leaves the original IP header unencrypted so the packet can be routed end-to-end.
Incorrect. ESP gives confidentiality in both modes by encrypting the payload. The mode only changes how much of the packet gets encrypted, not whether encryption happens at all.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not an essential process area for the Repeatable phase of the Software Capability Maturity Model (SW-CMM)?
questions.explanation: In level 2, the Repeatable level of the SW-CMM, the organization introduces basic life cycle management processes. Reuse of code in an organized fashion begins, and repeatable results are expected from similar projects. The crucial process areas for this level include Requirements Management, Software Project Planning, Software Project Tracking and Oversight, Software Subcontract Management, Software Quality Assurance, and Software Configuration Management. Software Quality Management is a process that occurs during level 4, the Managed stage of the SW-CMM.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Software Project Planning is one of the key process areas of Level 2 (Repeatable), where basic life cycle management processes are introduced. So it is an essential Repeatable-phase area.
Correct. Software Quality Management belongs to Level 4 (Managed), not Level 2. Don't confuse it with Software Quality Assurance, which is a Level 2 process area.
Incorrect. Software Project Tracking (and Oversight) is a key process area at Level 2. It helps make results repeatable across similar projects.
Incorrect. Software Subcontract Management is on the book's list of key process areas for the Repeatable level. That means it is an essential Level 2 area, not the exception.

questions.stem: Ben wants to provide predictive information about his organization's risk exposure in an automated way as part of an ongoing organizational risk management plan. What should he use to do this?
questions.explanation: Key risk indicators (KRIs) are often used to monitor risk for organizations that establish an ongoing risk management program. Using automated data gathering and tools that allow data to be digested and summarized can provide predictive information about how organizational risks are changing. KPIs are key performance indicators, which are used to assess how an organization is performing. Quantitative risk assessments are good for point-in-time views with detailed valuation and measurement-based risk assessments, whereas a penetration test would provide details of how well an organization's security controls are working.
optionNotes: Correct. Key risk indicators are made for ongoing risk monitoring. Automated data gathering and summarization lets them predict how organizational risk is changing, which is exactly what Ben needs.
Incorrect. Quantitative risk assessments give detailed, measurement-based valuations, but only as a point-in-time snapshot. They don't provide ongoing, automated predictive monitoring.
Incorrect. Key performance indicators measure how well the organization is performing against its goals. They don't indicate changing risk exposure.
Incorrect. A penetration test shows how well security controls hold up during a specific engagement. It is not a continuous, predictive measure of overall risk exposure.

questions.stem:
In the image shown here, what does system B send to system A at step 2 of the three-way TCP handshake?
[Figure, described in text: system A sends message 1 to system B; system B sends message 2 back to system A; system A then sends message 3 to system B.]
questions.explanation: The three-way handshake is SYN, SYN/ACK, ACK. System B should respond with “Synchronize and Acknowledge” to System A after it receives a SYN.
optionNotes: Incorrect. SYN is step 1: system A sends it to start the connection. At step 2, B has to acknowledge A's SYN as well as send its own synchronize, so a bare SYN isn't enough.
Incorrect. A plain ACK is step 3: system A sends it to acknowledge B's SYN/ACK and finish the handshake. B doesn't send it at step 2.
Incorrect. FIN/ACK is used to close a TCP session, not to set one up. It never appears in the three-way handshake (SYN, SYN/ACK, ACK).
Correct. After receiving A's SYN, system B replies with SYN/ACK (synchronize and acknowledge). This is step 2 of the SYN, SYN/ACK, ACK sequence.

questions.stem: Chris is conducting reconnaissance on a remote target and discovers that pings are allowed through his target's border firewall. What can he learn by using pings to probe the remote network?
options: Which systems respond to pings, a rough network topology, and potentially the location of additional firewalls
A list of all of the systems behind the target's firewall
The hostnames and time to live (TTL) for each pingable system and the ICMP types allowed through the firewall
Router advertisements, echo request responses, and potentially which hosts are tarpitted
questions.explanation: Systems that respond to pings will show the time to live for packets that reach them. Since TTL is decremented at each hop, this can help build a rough network topology map. In addition, some firewalls respond differently to pings than a normal system, which means pinging a network can sometimes reveal the presence of firewalls that would otherwise be invisible. Hostnames are revealed by a DNS lookup, and ICMP types allowed through a firewall are not revealed by only performing a ping. ICMP can be used for router advertisements, but pinging won't show them!
optionNotes: Correct. Hosts that reply show which systems answer pings, the TTL values (decremented each hop) help sketch a rough topology, and firewalls that respond differently can give away devices that would otherwise stay hidden.
Incorrect. Ping only finds hosts that answer ICMP echo requests. Systems that block or drop pings stay hidden, so it can't give a complete list of every system behind the firewall.
Incorrect. Ping does show TTL, but hostnames come from a DNS lookup, not from ping. Pinging alone also doesn't tell you which ICMP types the firewall lets through.
Incorrect. ICMP carries router advertisements, but pinging doesn't reveal them. Ping uses echo requests and replies only, and it won't reliably show which hosts are tarpitted.

questions.stem: Jake is conducting a review of his organization's identity and access management program. During his review, he is verifying the privileges assigned to each user and ensuring that they match with business requirements. What element of the program is he reviewing?
questions.explanation: Authorization defines what a subject can or can't do. Identification occurs when a subject claims an identity, accounting is provided by the logs and audit trail that track what occurs on a system, and authentication occurs when that identity is validated.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Identification is when a subject claims an identity, such as entering a username. It has nothing to do with checking which privileges each user holds.
Incorrect. Accounting comes from logs and audit trails that record what happens on a system. Jake is reviewing what users are allowed to do, not a record of what they did.
Correct. Authorization defines what a subject can or can't do. Checking each user's assigned privileges against business requirements is a review of authorization.
Incorrect. Authentication validates a claimed identity, for example with a password or token. It confirms who the user is, not which privileges they have.

questions.stem: Faith is looking at the /etc/passwd file on a system configured to use shadowed passwords. When she examines a line in the file for a user with interactive login permissions, what should she expect to see in the password field?
questions.explanation: When a system uses shadowed passwords, the hashed password value is stored in /etc/shadow instead of /etc/passwd. The /etc/passwd file would not contain the password in plaintext or hashed form. Instead, it would contain an x to indicate that the password hash is in the shadow file. The * character is normally used to disable interactive logins to an account.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Plaintext passwords are never stored in /etc/passwd. With shadowing, no form of the password appears there at all.
Incorrect. Shadowing moves the password hash out of the world-readable /etc/passwd and into /etc/shadow, so no hash appears in the passwd file.
Correct. An 'x' in the password field means the user's password hash is stored in the /etc/shadow file.
Incorrect. A '*' is normally used to disable interactive logins to an account. This user is allowed to log in interactively, so '*' would not appear.

questions.explanation: The log entries show the characteristic pattern of a port scan. The attacking system sends connection attempts to the target system against a series of commonly used ports.
optionNotes: Incorrect. SQL injection puts malicious SQL into application input and would appear in web or database logs. Firewall entries showing dropped TCP connections across many ports don't fit it.

Correct. This is correct. One source (192.168.250.4) makes a series of connection attempts to the same target, one after another, against common ports (21, 22, 23, 25, 53, 80, 110, 111). That is the classic pattern of a port scan.
Incorrect. Teardrop sends overlapping or malformed packet fragments that the target can't reassemble. These logs show ordinary TCP attempts to different ports, not fragment abuse.

Incorrect. A Land attack sends a SYN packet with the same source and destination IP address (and port). Here the source and destination addresses are different and the destination port changes each time.

questions.stem: Danielle is testing tax software, and part of her testing process requires her to input a variety of actual tax forms to verify that the software produces the right answers. What type of testing is Danielle performing?
questions.explanation: Testing for desired functionality is use-case testing. Dynamic testing is used to determine how code handles variables that change over time. Misuse testing focuses on how code handles examples of misuse, and fuzzing feeds unexpected data as an input to see how the code responds.
optionNotes: Correct. Danielle feeds real tax forms in and checks that the software gives the expected answers. That tests the intended functionality, which is what use-case testing does.
Incorrect. Dynamic testing runs the code to see how it handles variables that change over time. Danielle is checking expected results for normal use cases, not runtime behavior as variables change.
Incorrect. Fuzzing feeds unexpected or random data into a program to see how it responds. Danielle is using valid, actual tax forms, which is the opposite of fuzzing.
Incorrect. Misuse testing looks at how code handles abuse or improper use. Danielle is checking correct results from legitimate inputs, not misuse cases.

questions.stem: After 10 years working in her organization, Cassandra is moving into her fourth role, this time as a manager in the accounting department. What issue is likely to show up during an account review if her organization does not have strong account maintenance practices?
questions.explanation: Privilege creep is a common problem when employees change roles over time and their privileges and permissions are not properly modified to reflect their new roles. Least privilege issues are a design or implementation problem, and switching roles isn't typically what causes them to occur. Account creep is not a common industry term, and account termination would imply that someone has removed her account instead of switching her to new groups or new roles.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Least privilege violations are a design or implementation problem with how access is granted, not the usual result of someone moving through several roles over time.

Correct. Privilege creep happens when an employee changes roles and the permissions from earlier jobs are never removed. With four roles in 10 years and weak account maintenance, Cassandra has probably built up access she no longer needs.
Incorrect. 'Account creep' is not a standard industry term. The problem here is permissions piling up on one account, not extra accounts appearing.
Incorrect. Account termination would mean her account was removed. She is moving to a new role, so her account should be reassigned to new groups or roles, not deleted.

questions.stem: IP addresses like 10.10.10.10 and 172.19.24.21 are both examples of what type of IP address?
questions.explanation: These are examples of private IP addresses. RFC 1918 defines a set of private IP addresses for use in internal networks. These private addresses including 10.0.0.0 to 10.255.255.255, 172.16.0.0 to 172.31.255.255, and 192.168.0.0 to 192.168.255.255 should never be routable on the public Internet.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Both addresses sit inside the RFC 1918 reserved blocks (10.0.0.0/8 and 172.16.0.0/12). Those blocks are not supposed to be routed on the public Internet, so these addresses can't be public.

Incorrect. "Prohibited IP addresses" isn't a standard address category. Filters may block particular addresses, such as known-malicious IPs on a block list or spoofed sources, but that is a firewall policy decision, not a type of address.
Correct. RFC 1918 reserves 10.0.0.0–10.255.255.255, 172.16.0.0–172.31.255.255 and 192.168.0.0–192.168.255.255 for internal networks. Both example addresses fall inside these private ranges.

Incorrect. Under classful addressing, 10.10.10.10 is a Class A address (first octet 1–126). Only 172.19.24.21 is Class B, so "Class B" doesn't describe both addresses. What they share is that both are RFC 1918 private addresses.

questions.stem: Ben is reviewing the password recovery mechanism used by his website and discovers that the approach uses cognitive authentication through the use of security questions. What is the major issue with this approach?
options: It prevents the use of tokens.
The question's answer may be easy to find on the Internet.
Cognitive passwords require users to think to answer the question, and not all users may be able to solve the problems presented.
Cognitive passwords don't support long passwords.
questions.explanation: A cognitive password authenticates users based on a series of facts or answers to questions that they know. Preset questions for cognitive passwords typically rely on common information about a user like their mother's maiden name or the name of their pet, and that information can frequently be found on the Internet. The best cognitive password systems let users make up their own questions.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Security questions are a knowledge factor and don't stop anyone from also using tokens (an ownership factor) for MFA or recovery. Using one doesn't block the other.
Correct. Preset cognitive questions often ask about things like a mother's maiden name or a pet's name. Attackers can often find these answers online or through social media.
Incorrect. Cognitive questions ask for personal facts the user already knows. They aren't puzzles to solve, so how well a user can solve problems isn't the issue.
Incorrect. Answer length isn't the main weakness of cognitive passwords, and nothing in how they work stops answers from being long. The real problem is that the answers can be guessed or researched.

questions.stem: Megan needs to create a forensic copy of a hard drive that will be used in an investigation. Which of the following tools is best suited to her work?
questions.explanation: The Linux tool dd creates a bit-by-bit copy of the target drive that is well suited to forensic use, and special forensic versions of dd exist that can provide even more forensic features. Simply copying files using a tool like xcopy does not create a forensically sound copy. DBAN is a drive wiping tool and would cause Megan to lose the data she is seeking to copy. ImageMagick is a graphics manipulation and editing program.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Xcopy only copies files at the file-system level. It misses slack space, unallocated space, and deleted data, so it can't make a forensically sound image.
Correct. Dd makes a bit-by-bit copy of the whole drive, which is what forensic imaging requires. Forensic variants of dd, such as dcfldd, add extra features like hashing.
Incorrect. DBAN (Darik's Boot and Nuke) is a drive-wiping tool. Running it would destroy the evidence Megan is trying to preserve.
Incorrect. ImageMagick is a program for editing and converting graphics. Despite the word "image" in its name, it has nothing to do with disk imaging.

questions.stem: Kay is selecting an application management approach for her organization. Employees need the flexibility to install software on their systems, but Kay wants to prevent them from installing certain prohibited packages. What type of approach should she use?
questions.explanation: The blacklist approach to application control blocks certain prohibited packages but allows the installation of other software on systems. The whitelist approach uses the reverse philosophy and allows only approved software. Antivirus software would detect the installation of malicious software only after the fact. Heuristic detection is a variant of antivirus software.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Antivirus looks for malicious code and only catches malware once it is being installed. It can't stop users from installing legitimate software that the company has prohibited.
Incorrect. A whitelist does the opposite of what Kay wants: it allows only approved software. That takes away the flexibility employees need to install other packages.
Correct. A blacklist blocks only the specific prohibited packages and lets users install anything else, which is exactly what Kay needs.
Incorrect. Heuristic detection is a kind of antivirus scanning that spots malware by its behavior. It isn't a way to control which applications are allowed.

questions.stem: Donna is a security administrator for a healthcare provider located in the United States and is reviewing their payment processing system. It contains data relating to the past, present, or future payment for the provision of healthcare to an individual. How would this information be classified under HIPAA?
questions.explanation: Protected health information (PHI) is specifically defined by HIPAA to include information about an individual's medical bills. PCI could refer to the payment card industry's security standard but would apply only in relation to payment cards. PII is a broadly defined term for personally identifiable information, and personal billing data isn't a broadly used industry term.
optionNotes: Incorrect. PCI refers to the Payment Card Industry standard (PCI DSS), which covers payment card data only, not HIPAA's classification of healthcare payment information.
Incorrect. Personal billing data is not a term HIPAA defines, and the industry doesn't really use it. HIPAA classifies healthcare payment information as PHI.
Correct. HIPAA's definition of protected health information explicitly covers information about past, present, or future payment for an individual's healthcare, such as medical bills.
Incorrect. PII is a broad, general term for personally identifiable information. It is not the specific HIPAA category for healthcare payment information, which is PHI.

questions.stem: Harold's company has a strong password policy that requires a minimum length of 12 characters and the use of both alphanumeric characters and symbols. What technique would be the most effective way for an attacker to compromise passwords in Harold's organization?
questions.explanation: A social engineering attack may trick a user into revealing their password to the attacker. Other attacks that depend on guessing passwords, such as brute-force attacks, rainbow table attacks, and dictionary attacks, are unlikely to be successful in light of the organization's strong password policy.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Brute force has to try every possible combination. With a 12-character minimum and a mixed character set, the keyspace is too large for this to succeed in practical time.
Incorrect. A dictionary attack tries common words and their variants. Complex 12-character passwords with symbols are unlikely to show up in a wordlist, so this attack is unlikely to work.
Incorrect. Rainbow tables are precomputed hash lookups, and they become impractically large for long passwords that mix character types. The strong policy makes this attack unlikely to succeed.
Correct. Social engineering gets around password strength completely by tricking users into revealing their passwords. That makes it the most effective option against a strong password policy.

questions.stem: While traveling, James is held at knifepoint and forced to log into his laptop. What is this called?
questions.explanation: When someone is forced to perform an action under threat, it is known as duress.
optionNotes: Correct. Duress is being forced to do something against your will under threat, such as logging into a laptop at knifepoint. That is exactly James's situation.

Incorrect. "Antisocial engineering" isn't a recognized security term. Social engineering works by manipulating or deceiving people, not by threatening them with a weapon, so the made-up name doesn't describe this.
Incorrect. Distress describes the alarm or call for help, such as a duress button that sends a distress call to a monitoring entity. It isn't the name for being coerced under threat.
Incorrect. "Knifepoint hacking" is a made-up term. The standard term for being forced to act under threat, whether at gunpoint or knifepoint, is duress.

questions.stem: Kayla recently took a position at a new start-up company that runs entirely in the cloud. The company leverages a major IaaS provider for hosting its web services and a SaaS email system. Both of these providers operate multitenant environments. What term best describes the type of cloud environment this organization uses?
questions.explanation: The term that best describes the type of cloud environment used by Kayla's company, which leverages a major IaaS provider for hosting its web services and a SaaS email system operating in multitenant environments, is a public cloud. A public cloud is where the services are delivered over the public Internet and shared across different organizations. A dedicated cloud, also known as a private cloud, is operated solely for one organization, and this is not the case for Kayla's company. A private cloud is infrastructure operated solely for a single organization, whether managed internally or by a third-party, and hosted either internally or externally, which also does not apply here. A hybrid cloud is a composition of two or more cloud delivery models (private, community, or public) that remain distinct entities but are bound together, offering the benefits of multiple deployment models, which again does not match the company's use of exclusively public cloud services.
optionNotes: Correct. Both the IaaS provider and the SaaS email service are multitenant and delivered over the public Internet to many organizations, so this is a public cloud.
Incorrect. A dedicated cloud is another name for a private cloud, which serves only one organization. Kayla's providers share their infrastructure among many tenants.
Incorrect. A private cloud is run for a single organization, whether managed internally or by a third party. Multitenant IaaS and SaaS services don't fit that description.
Incorrect. A hybrid cloud ties two or more deployment models together, such as private plus public. This company uses only public cloud services, so there is nothing to combine.

questions.stem:
Cameron is responsible for backing up his company's primary file server. He configured a backup schedule that performs full backups every Monday evening at 9 p.m. and incremental backups on other days of the week at that same time. How many files will be copied in Wednesday's backup?
[Exhibit, transcribed from the book's figure:]
File Modifications
Monday 8AM - File 1 created
Monday 10AM - File 2 created
Monday 11AM - File 3 created
Monday 4PM - File 1 modified
Monday 5PM - File 4 created
Tuesday 8AM - File 1 modified
Tuesday 9AM - File 2 modified
Tuesday 10AM - File 5 created
Wednesday 8AM - File 3 modified
Wednesday 9AM - File 6 created
questions.explanation: In this scenario, all of the files on the server will be backed up on Monday evening during the full backup. Tuesday's incremental backup will include all files changed since Monday's full backup: files 1, 2, and 5. Wednesday's incremental backup will then include all files modified since Tuesday's incremental backup: files 3 and 6. Therefore, only two files are included in Wednesday's incremental backup.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Only one file would be right if you missed one of Wednesday's changes. Both File 3 (modified) and File 6 (created) changed after Tuesday's 9 p.m. incremental, so both get copied.
Correct. An incremental backup copies only what changed since the last backup, which here is Tuesday's incremental. Files 3 and 6 changed Wednesday morning, so two files are copied.

Incorrect. Five files is what a differential backup would copy on Wednesday: everything changed since Monday's full backup (Files 1, 2, 3, 5, 6). An incremental resets the baseline each night, so Tuesday's changes aren't copied again.

Incorrect. Six files would mean copying every file on the server as of Wednesday, like a full backup. Wednesday's incremental copies only files changed since Tuesday's backup, which are Files 3 and 6.

questions.stem: Susan uses a SPAN port to monitor traffic to her production website and uses a monitoring tool to identify performance issues in real time. What type of monitoring is she conducting?
questions.explanation: Susan is performing passive monitoring, which uses a network tap or SPAN port to capture traffic to analyze it without impacting the network or devices that it is used to monitor. Synthetic, or active, monitoring uses recorded or generated traffic to test for performance and other issues. Signature-based technologies include IDS, IPS, and antimalware systems.
optionNotes: Correct. A SPAN port or network tap copies real user traffic so it can be analyzed without affecting the network or the systems being watched. That is passive monitoring.
Incorrect. Active monitoring sends recorded or generated traffic to test performance. Susan is only watching copies of real traffic from a SPAN port, so she isn't generating any.
Incorrect. Synthetic monitoring is another name for active monitoring. It replays or generates transactions to test the site, while Susan is observing real user traffic.
Incorrect. Signature-based monitoring is a detection method used by IDS, IPS and antimalware tools to spot known threats. It isn't a type of performance monitoring of mirrored traffic.

questions.stem: In what type of attack do attackers manage to insert themselves into a connection between a user and a legitimate website?
questions.explanation: In a man-in-the-middle attack, attackers manage to insert themselves into a connection between a user and a legitimate website, relaying traffic between the two parties while eavesdropping on the connection. Although similarly named, the meet-in-the-middle attack is a cryptographic attack that does not necessarily involve connection tampering. Fraggle is a network-based denial-of-service attack using UDP packets. Wardriving is a reconnaissance technique for discovering open or weakly secured wireless networks.
optionNotes: Correct. In a man-in-the-middle attack, the attacker sits in the connection between the user and the legitimate site. They relay traffic both ways and eavesdrop on it.
Incorrect. Fraggle is a network denial-of-service attack that floods a target with UDP packets. It overwhelms the target and doesn't intercept or relay a user's connection.
Incorrect. Wardriving is a reconnaissance technique: you move around looking for open or weakly secured wireless networks. It's not about inserting yourself into a live session.
Incorrect. The name is a trap. Meet-in-the-middle is a cryptographic attack, for example against double encryption like 2DES. It doesn't necessarily involve tampering with a connection.

questions.stem: Which one of the following would be considered an example of infrastructure-as-a-service cloud computing?
options: Payroll system managed by a vendor and delivered over the web
Application platform managed by a vendor that runs customer code
Servers provisioned by customers on a vendor-managed virtualization platform
Web-based email service provided by a vendor
questions.explanation: One of the core capabilities of infrastructure as a service is providing servers on a vendor-managed virtualization platform. Web-based payroll and email systems are examples of software as a service. An application platform managed by a vendor that runs customer code is an example of platform as a service.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A vendor-managed payroll application delivered over the web is software as a service (SaaS). The customer just uses the finished application and manages none of the infrastructure.
Incorrect. A vendor-managed application platform that runs customer code is platform as a service (PaaS). The customer supplies code, not servers or operating systems.
Correct. Under IaaS, customers provision and manage their own servers on a virtualization platform the vendor manages. This is a core IaaS capability.
Incorrect. Web-based email from a vendor is a complete application the customer consumes, so it is software as a service (SaaS), not IaaS.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
Darcy is an information security risk analyst for Roscommon Agricultural Products. She is currently trying to decide whether the company should purchase an upgraded fire suppression system for their primary data center. The data center facility has a replacement cost of $2 million. After consulting with actuaries, data center managers, and fire subject-matter experts, Darcy determined that a typical fire would likely require the replacement of all equipment inside the building but not cause significant structural damage. Together, they estimated that recovering from the fire would cost $750,000. They also determined that the company can expect a fire of this magnitude once every 50 years.

Based on the information in this scenario, what is the exposure factor for the effect of a fire on the Roscommon Agricultural Products data center?
questions.explanation: The exposure factor is the percentage of the facility that risk managers expect will be damaged if a risk materializes. It is calculated by dividing the amount of damage by the asset value. In this case, that is $750,000 in damage divided by the $2 million facility value, or 37.5%.
optionNotes: Incorrect. 7.5% doesn't come from dividing the $750,000 loss by the $2 million asset value, so it can't be the EF. It looks like a decimal-place slip, possibly from 0.0375 or from dividing by $10 million.
Incorrect. Exposure factor is the expected damage as a percentage of the asset's value. Dividing $750,000 by $2 million gives 37.5%, not 15%, so 15% is a miscalculation.
Incorrect. 27.5% doesn't match the EF formula (damage ÷ asset value). The correct result is $750,000 / $2,000,000 = 37.5%.
Correct. EF is the expected damage divided by the asset value: $750,000 / $2,000,000 = 37.5%.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
Darcy is an information security risk analyst for Roscommon Agricultural Products. She is currently trying to decide whether the company should purchase an upgraded fire suppression system for their primary data center. The data center facility has a replacement cost of $2 million. After consulting with actuaries, data center managers, and fire subject-matter experts, Darcy determined that a typical fire would likely require the replacement of all equipment inside the building but not cause significant structural damage. Together, they estimated that recovering from the fire would cost $750,000. They also determined that the company can expect a fire of this magnitude once every 50 years.

Based on the information in this scenario, what is the annualized rate of occurrence for a fire at the Roscommon Agricultural Products data center?
questions.explanation: The annualized rate of occurrence is the number of times each year that risk analysts expect a risk to happen. In this case, the analysts expect fires will occur once every 50 years, or 0.02 times per year.
optionNotes: Incorrect. 0.002 would mean one fire every 500 years. That shifts the decimal one place too far from the scenario's once-every-50-years estimate.
Incorrect. 0.005 works out to one fire every 200 years. The rate should come from 1 ÷ 50, which gives 0.02.
Correct. ARO is how many times per year the risk is expected to happen. One fire every 50 years means 1/50 = 0.02 per year.
Incorrect. 0.05 would mean one fire every 20 years, so it overstates the frequency. ARO here is 1/50 = 0.02. ALE is SLE × ARO, so it is a separate figure from the rate itself.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
Darcy is an information security risk analyst for Roscommon Agricultural Products. She is currently trying to decide whether the company should purchase an upgraded fire suppression system for their primary data center. The data center facility has a replacement cost of $2 million. After consulting with actuaries, data center managers, and fire subject-matter experts, Darcy determined that a typical fire would likely require the replacement of all equipment inside the building but not cause significant structural damage. Together, they estimated that recovering from the fire would cost $750,000. They also determined that the company can expect a fire of this magnitude once every 50 years.

Based on the information in this scenario, what is the annualized loss expectancy for a fire at the Roscommon Agricultural Products data center?
questions.explanation: The annualized loss expectancy is calculated by multiplying the single loss expectancy (SLE) by the annualized rate of occurrence (ARO). In this case, the SLE is $750,000, and the ARO is 0.02. Multiplying these numbers together gives you the ALE of $15,000.
optionNotes: Correct. ALE = SLE × ARO. The SLE is $750,000 and a fire once every 50 years gives an ARO of 0.02, so $750,000 × 0.02 = $15,000.
Incorrect. $25,000 doesn't come from SLE × ARO. It is roughly what you get by dividing $750,000 by 30 instead of 50, or by misusing the $2 million facility value.
Incorrect. $75,000 would mean an ARO of 0.1 (one fire every 10 years). The scenario says one fire every 50 years, so the ARO is 0.02.
Incorrect. $750,000 is the single loss expectancy (the cost of one fire). It still has to be multiplied by the ARO of 0.02 to get the annualized figure.

questions.stem: Which one of the following techniques uses statistical methods to select a small number of log records from a large pool for further analysis with the goal of choosing a set of records that is representative of the entire pool?
questions.explanation: The two main methods of choosing records from a large pool for further analysis are sampling and clipping. Sampling uses statistical techniques to choose a sample that is representative of the entire pool, while clipping uses threshold values to select those records that exceed a predefined threshold because they may be of most interest to analysts.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Clipping does not use statistics. It picks records whose values go over a set threshold because those are likely to interest analysts, so the records it keeps are not representative of the whole pool.

Incorrect. Randomization is not a named log-reduction technique. Random selection can be one part of how a sample is drawn, but the technique that statistically picks a representative subset of logs is called sampling.
Correct. Sampling uses statistical techniques to choose a small subset of log records that is representative of the entire pool, so analysts can work with less data.
Incorrect. Selection is a generic word, not a recognized log analysis method. The two named methods for reducing log records are sampling and clipping.

questions.stem: Mike wants to ensure that third-party users of his service's API can be tracked to prevent abuse of the API. What should he implement to help with this?
questions.explanation: API keys, or application programming interface keys, are passed to services and identify the program, developer, or user. With this information, Mike can programmatically control API usage per user. Of course, if the keys are inadvertently exposed, the API keys themselves could be abused. Session IDs are typically used to identify users of an application, not an API. API firewalls and API buffers were made up for this question.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Session IDs usually track a user's session inside an application, not a third-party program calling an API, so they can't control API usage per caller.
Incorrect. The book made up "API firewall" for this question. It is not a standard way to identify and track individual API consumers.
Correct. An API key is sent with every request and identifies the program, developer, or user, so Mike can track and limit API usage per user. Keys that leak can themselves be abused.
Incorrect. The book made up "API buffer" for this question. It does nothing to identify or track third-party API users.

questions.stem: Fran is a web developer who works for an online retailer. Her boss asked her to create a way that customers can easily integrate themselves with Fran's company's site. They need to be able to check inventory in real time, place orders, and check order status programmatically without having to access the web page. What can Fran create to most directly facilitate this interaction?
questions.explanation: An application programming interface (API) allows external users to directly call routines within Fran's code. They can embed API calls within scripts and other programs to automate interactions with Fran's company. A web scraper or call center might facilitate the same tasks, but they do not do so in a direct integration. Data dictionaries might provide useful information, but they also do not allow direct integration.
optionNotes: Correct. An API lets external customers call Fran's code directly from their own scripts and programs, so they can check inventory, place orders, and check order status automatically without using the web page.
Incorrect. A web scraper pulls data out of rendered web pages. It still relies on the web interface and is not a direct programmatic integration, and it can't reliably place orders.
Incorrect. A data dictionary describes data elements and their meaning. It may be useful documentation, but customers can't use it to run transactions or integrate directly.
Incorrect. A call center lets customers do these tasks through human agents. That is manual work, not programmatic integration.

questions.stem: Todd's data center facility recently experienced a series of events that involved the momentary loss of power. What term best describes these events?
questions.explanation: A fault is a momentary loss of power. Blackouts are sustained complete losses of power. Sags and brownouts are not complete power disruptions but rather periods of low-voltage conditions.
optionNotes: Correct. A fault is a momentary, complete loss of power, which matches the brief outages Todd's facility had.
Incorrect. A blackout is a sustained (prolonged) complete loss of power. These events were only momentary, so blackout doesn't fit.
Incorrect. A sag is a momentary drop to low voltage, not a complete loss of power. Power was actually lost here, so sag is wrong.
Incorrect. A brownout is a prolonged period of low voltage. It is neither momentary nor a complete loss of power.

questions.stem: Lauren's team of system administrators each deals with hundreds of systems with varying levels of security requirements and finds it difficult to handle the multitude of usernames and passwords they each have. What type of solution should she recommend to ensure that passwords are properly handled and that features like logging and password rotation occur?
questions.explanation: Lauren's team would benefit from a credential management system. Credential management systems offer features like password management, multifactor authentication to retrieve passwords, logging, audit, and password rotation capabilities. A strong password policy would only make maintenance of passwords for many systems a more difficult task if done manually. Single sign-on would help if all the systems had the same sensitivity levels, but different credentials are normally required for higher-sensitivity systems.
optionNotes: Correct. A credential management system (password vault) stores the many credentials securely and adds MFA to retrieve passwords, logging, auditing and automatic password rotation, which are exactly the features Lauren needs.

Incorrect. A strong password policy only sets rules for password complexity and length. Without a tool to manage them, it makes keeping track of passwords on hundreds of systems harder, and it gives no logging or rotation.
Incorrect. Separation of duties splits critical tasks between people to prevent fraud and errors. It doesn't help admins store, log or rotate the many credentials they hold.

Incorrect. Single sign-on lets one credential work across many systems. That only fits when the systems have similar sensitivity. Higher-sensitivity systems usually need their own credentials, and SSO doesn't provide password rotation.

questions.stem:
Ed's Windows system can't connect to the network, and ipconfig shows the following:
[Exhibit, transcribed from the book's figure:]
Ethernet adapter Local Area Connection:
   Connection-specific DNS Suffix  . :
   Link-local IPv6 Address . . . . . : fe80::90f1:e9f0:c0f5:b0ba%11
   IPv4 Address. . . . . . . . . . . : 169.254.19.21
   Subnet Mask . . . . . . . . . . . : 255.255.0.0
   Default Gateway . . . . . . . . . :
What has occurred on the system?
options: The system has been assigned an invalid IP address by its DHCP server.
The system has a manually assigned IP address.
The system has failed to get a DHCP address and has assigned itself an address.
The subnet mask is set incorrectly, and the system cannot communicate with the gateway.
questions.explanation: Windows systems will assign themselves an APIPA address between 169.254.0.1 and 169.254.255.254 if they cannot contact a DHCP server.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A DHCP server doesn't hand out 169.254.x.x addresses. That range is APIPA, which a Windows client gives itself when it can't reach any DHCP server.

Incorrect. 169.254.19.21 with a /16 mask and no gateway is the typical APIPA self-assignment, not a static configuration. An administrator setting the address by hand would normally also set a gateway.
Correct. If Windows can't contact a DHCP server, it gives itself an APIPA address between 169.254.0.1 and 169.254.255.254, which is exactly what this output shows.
Incorrect. 255.255.0.0 is the normal mask for an APIPA address, so the mask is not the problem. There is no gateway at all because the DHCP request failed.

questions.stem: Gina is performing the initial creation of user accounts for a batch of new employees. What phase of the provisioning process is she conducting?
questions.explanation: Enrollment, or registration, is the initial creation of a user account in the provisioning process. Clearance verification and background checks are sometimes part of the process that ensures that the identity of the person being enrolled matches who they claim to be. Initialization is not used to describe the provisioning process.
optionNotes: Correct. Enrollment (also called registration) is the step where a user account is first created during provisioning, which is exactly what Gina is doing for the new hires.
Incorrect. Clearance verification can be part of confirming that the person being enrolled is who they claim to be. It is a supporting identity check, not the phase where accounts are created.
Incorrect. Background checks sometimes back up identity proofing before or during enrollment. They do not create accounts and are not a named phase of provisioning.
Incorrect. Initialization is not a term used for any phase of the provisioning process. It is a plausible-sounding distractor.

questions.stem: Ravi is developing procedures for forensic investigations conducted by his organization and would like to differentiate based upon the evidentiary standards commonly used for each type of investigation. What type of forensic investigation typically has the highest evidentiary standards?
questions.explanation: Criminal forensic investigations typically have the highest standards for evidence, as they must be able to help prove the case beyond a reasonable doubt. Administrative investigations merely need to meet the standards of the organization and to be able to be defended in court, while civil investigations operate on a preponderance of evidence. There is not a category of forensic investigation referred to as “industry” in the CISSP exam's breakdown of forensic types.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Administrative investigations only have to satisfy the organization's own standards and hold up if challenged in court. That is a far lower bar than criminal proof.
Correct. Criminal investigations need evidence strong enough to prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt, which is the highest standard of the investigation types.
Incorrect. Civil investigations use the preponderance-of-evidence standard, which means 'more likely than not.' That is lower than beyond a reasonable doubt.
Incorrect. 'Industry' isn't one of the forensic investigation types in the CISSP breakdown, so it has no evidentiary standard of its own to compare.

questions.stem: What U.S. legal protection prevents law enforcement agencies from searching an American facility or electronic system without either probable cause or consent?
questions.explanation: The Fourth Amendment states, in part, that “the right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers and effects, against unreasonable searches and seizures, shall not be violated, and no Warrants shall issue, but upon probable cause, supported by Oath or affirmation, and particularly describing the place to be searched, and the persons or things to be seized.” The First Amendment contains protections related to freedom of speech. The Fifth Amendment ensures that no person will be required to serve as a witness against themselves. The Fifteenth Amendment protects the voting rights of citizens.
optionNotes: Incorrect. The First Amendment protects freedom of speech, religion, press, and assembly. It says nothing about searches or seizures.
Correct. The Fourth Amendment bars unreasonable searches and seizures and requires probable cause before a warrant is issued. Courts have applied it to facilities and electronic systems.
Incorrect. The Fifth Amendment protects people from being forced to testify against themselves. It does not cover searching premises or systems.
Incorrect. The Fifteenth Amendment protects citizens' voting rights. It has nothing to do with law enforcement searches.

questions.stem: Tom believes that a customer of his Internet service provider has been exploiting a vulnerability in his system to read the email messages of other customers. If true, what law did the customer most likely violate?
questions.explanation: The Electronic Communications Privacy Act (ECPA) makes it a crime to invade the electronic privacy of an individual. It prohibits the unauthorized monitoring of email and voicemail communications.
optionNotes: Correct. ECPA makes invading an individual's electronic privacy a crime and specifically bans unauthorized monitoring of email and voicemail. A customer reading other customers' email fits that directly.

Incorrect. CALEA requires telecom carriers and ISPs to build in wiretap capability for lawful law-enforcement intercepts. It puts duties on providers and doesn't criminalize a customer reading someone else's email.
Incorrect. HITECH extends HIPAA's privacy and security rules and adds breach-notification requirements for health information. Nothing here involves protected health information.
Incorrect. The Privacy Act of 1974 limits how federal government agencies collect and disclose personal records. It doesn't cover a private ISP customer snooping on email.

questions.stem:
In the protection ring model shown here, what ring contains user programs and applications?
[Figure, described in text: four concentric circles labeled RING 0 (innermost), RING 1, RING 2 and RING 3 (outermost).]
questions.explanation: The kernel lies within the central ring, Ring 0. Ring 1 contains other operating system components. Ring 2 is used for drivers and protocols. User-level programs and applications run at Ring 3. Rings 0–2 run in privileged mode, whereas Ring 3 runs in user mode.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Ring 0 is the innermost, most privileged ring. It holds the OS kernel, not user applications.
Incorrect. Ring 1 holds the other operating system components outside the kernel. It runs in privileged mode, so user programs don't belong there.
Incorrect. Ring 2 is used for device drivers and protocols. It is still privileged mode, not where user-level applications run.
Correct. Ring 3 is the outermost ring and runs in user mode. User-level programs and applications run here, with the least privilege.

questions.stem: In virtualization platforms, what name is given to the module that is responsible for controlling access to physical resources by virtual resources?
questions.explanation: The hypervisor runs within the virtualization platform and serves as the moderator between virtual resources and physical resources.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A guest machine is a virtual machine running on the hypervisor. It uses the virtualized resources and doesn't control access to the physical hardware.
Incorrect. Software-defined networking (SDN) separates network control from the network hardware. It is a networking approach, not the module that controls VM access to physical resources.

Incorrect. A kernel is the core of an operating system, and a security kernel enforces access control within one system. In virtualization, the hypervisor is the component that sits between the VMs and the physical hardware.
Correct. The hypervisor runs within the virtualization platform and moderates between virtual resources and physical resources, controlling each VM's access to the hardware.

questions.stem: In which cloud computing model does a customer share computing infrastructure with other customers of the cloud vendor where one customer may not know the other's identity?
questions.explanation: In the public cloud computing model, the vendor builds a single platform that is shared among many different customers. This is also known as the shared tenancy model.
optionNotes: Correct. Public cloud has the vendor run one platform shared by many unrelated customers (shared tenancy). Tenants usually don't know who else is on the same infrastructure.
Incorrect. A private cloud is dedicated to a single customer, whether it sits on-premises or in a provider's data center. No infrastructure is shared with unknown tenants.
Incorrect. A community cloud is shared by a known group with common needs, such as a group of hospitals. The members know each other, so it doesn't match anonymous sharing.

Incorrect. 'Shared cloud' isn't a standard cloud deployment model. The standard ones are public, private, community and hybrid. 'Shared tenancy' describes how public cloud works, not a separate model.

questions.stem: Justin recently participated in a disaster recovery plan test where the team sat together and discussed the response to a scenario but did not actually activate any disaster recovery controls. What type of test did he participate in?
questions.explanation: During a tabletop exercise, team members come together and walk through a scenario without making any changes to information systems. The read-through is the least disruptive type of disaster recovery test. During a read-through, team members each review the contents of their disaster recovery checklists on their own and suggest any necessary changes. During a parallel test, the team actually activates the disaster recovery site for testing, but the primary site remains operational. During a full interruption test, the team takes down the primary site and confirms that the disaster recovery site is capable of handling regular operations. The full interruption test is the most thorough test but also the most disruptive.
optionNotes: Incorrect. In a read-through, each team member reviews their own DR checklist separately and suggests changes. Nobody meets as a group to talk through a scenario.
Incorrect. A full interruption test shuts down the primary site and moves real operations to the DR site. It is the most disruptive test, but Justin's team activated no controls.
Incorrect. A parallel test brings the DR site online while the primary site keeps running. That means DR controls are activated, and this scenario rules that out.
Correct. In a tabletop exercise, the team meets and walks through a scenario together without changing any information systems or activating DR controls.

questions.stem: Susan wants to integrate her website to allow users to use accounts from sites like Google. What technology should she adopt?
questions.explanation: OpenID Connect is a widely supported standard that allows a user to use a single account to log into multiple sites, and Google accounts are frequently used with OpenID Connect.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Kerberos is a ticket-based SSO protocol for internal networks and realms, built around a KDC. It doesn't let users log into outside websites with Google accounts.
Incorrect. LDAP is a directory access protocol used for on-premises identity stores such as Active Directory. It doesn't provide federated web login through third-party providers like Google.
Correct. OpenID Connect is a widely supported authentication layer built on OAuth. It lets one account, often a Google account, log users into many websites, which is exactly what Susan needs.
Incorrect. SESAME is a European improvement on Kerberos for SSO across multi-vendor enterprise systems. It isn't used for consumer web login with Google accounts.

questions.stem: Tom is conducting a business continuity planning effort for Orange Blossoms, a fruit orchard located in Central Florida. During the assessment process, the committee determined that there is a small risk of snow in the region but that the cost of implementing controls to reduce the impact of that risk is not warranted. They elect to not take any specific action in response to the risk. What risk management strategy is Orange Blossoms pursuing?
questions.explanation: Risk acceptance occurs when an organization determines that the costs involved in pursuing other risk management strategies are not justified and they choose not to pursue any action.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Risk mitigation means putting controls in place to lower a risk's likelihood or impact. The committee decided controls weren't worth the cost and took no action, so nothing was mitigated.
Incorrect. Risk transference moves the financial impact to someone else, for example by buying insurance. Orange Blossoms did not shift the snow risk to any third party.

Incorrect. Risk avoidance removes the cause of the risk by picking a different activity or location, such as setting up in Arizona instead of Florida. The orchard stays where it is and keeps the snow risk.
Correct. Risk acceptance is when the organization decides other strategies cost more than they are worth and chooses to take no action. That is exactly what the committee did with the snow risk.

questions.stem: Paul is reviewing the contents of an audit report and discovers a finding that a manager in the accounting department has full access to perform every function in the financial system. What security principles have most likely been violated? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Accounting departments are normally required to separate sensitive duties, such as the ability to add a new vendor and issue a check. Allowing the manager to perform both of these actions would, therefore, violate the principle of separation of duties. Also, it is quite likely that the manager does not need all of these privileges to carry out their work, violating the principle of least privilege. There is no indication that the situation does not follow job rotation assignments or that the access was not properly granted and subject to a management review.
optionNotes: Correct. Accounting must split sensitive tasks like adding a vendor and issuing a check. When one manager can do every function, that split is gone, so separation of duties is violated.
Incorrect. Job rotation means moving staff through different positions over time. Nothing in the finding says rotation assignments were skipped.
Incorrect. Nothing suggests the access was granted improperly or skipped management review. The problem is how much access the manager has, not how it was approved.
Correct. The manager almost certainly doesn't need every function in the financial system to do their job. Having excess privileges violates least privilege.

questions.stem: Jack's organization is a multinational nonprofit that has small offices in many developing countries throughout the world. They need to implement an access control system that allows flexibility and that can work despite poor Internet connectivity at their locations. What is the best type of access control design for Jack's organization?
questions.explanation: Decentralized access control makes sense because it allows local control over access. When network connectivity to a central control point is a problem or if rules and regulations may vary significantly from location to location, centralized control can be less desirable than decentralized control despite its challenges with consistency. Since the problem does not describe specific control needs, mandatory access control and rule-based access controls could fit the need but aren't the best answer.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Centralized access control relies on a central control point, so poor Internet connectivity at remote offices would break or degrade access decisions. It's also less flexible when local rules differ.
Incorrect. Mandatory access control is a model built on classification labels. The scenario names no labeling or specific control requirement, and MAC does nothing to solve the connectivity problem.

Correct. Decentralized access control lets each office manage access locally, so it keeps working when the link to a central point is down. It also allows flexibility where rules vary by location, though at some cost to consistency.

Incorrect. Rule-based access control applies global rules, as firewalls do. The question gives no specific control needs that would call for it, and it doesn't address the poor connectivity, so it could fit but isn't the best answer.

questions.stem: What U.S. government classification label is applied to information that, if disclosed, could cause serious damage to national security and also requires that the damage that would be caused is able to be described or identified by the classification authority?
questions.explanation: The U.S. government classifies data that could reasonably be expected to cause damage to national security if disclosed, and for which the damage can be identified or described, as Secret. The U.S. government does not use Classified in its formal four levels of classification. Top Secret data could cause exceptionally grave damage, whereas Confidential data could be expected to cause damage.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Classified is a general term for any protected government information. It is not one of the formal U.S. classification levels, so it can't be the label tied to serious damage.

Correct. Secret is the label for information whose disclosure could reasonably be expected to cause serious damage to national security, where the classification authority can identify or describe that damage.

Incorrect. Confidential is the lowest classified level. It applies when disclosure could cause damage (not serious damage) to national security, so it sits one level below what the question describes.
Incorrect. Top Secret is the highest level. It is reserved for information whose disclosure could cause exceptionally grave damage, which is a step above the serious damage named in the question.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
Mike and Renee would like to use an asymmetric cryptosystem to communicate with each other. They are located in different parts of the country but have exchanged encryption keys by using digital certificates signed by a mutually trusted certificate authority.

When the certificate authority (CA) created Renee's digital certificate, what key was contained within the body of the certificate?
questions.explanation: The purpose of a digital certificate is to provide the general public with an authenticated copy of the certificate subject's public key.
optionNotes: Correct. A digital certificate exists to give the public an authenticated copy of the subject's public key. The body of Renee's certificate therefore holds Renee's public key, bound to her identity.
Incorrect. A private key is never placed in a certificate. Renee keeps it secret, and only her public key is bound to her identity and published.

Incorrect. The CA's public key isn't in the body of Renee's certificate. Relying parties already hold it, usually through the CA's own root certificate, and use it to verify the CA's signature on Renee's certificate.
Incorrect. The CA uses its private key to sign Renee's certificate. That key is never placed in a certificate, because exposing it would let anyone forge certificates.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
Mike and Renee would like to use an asymmetric cryptosystem to communicate with each other. They are located in different parts of the country but have exchanged encryption keys by using digital certificates signed by a mutually trusted certificate authority.

When the certificate authority created Renee's digital certificate, what key did it use to digitally sign the completed certificate?
questions.explanation: The last step of the certificate creation process is the digital signature. During this step, the certificate authority signs the certificate using its own private key.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Renee's public key is the subject key that gets embedded in the certificate. It is the content being certified, not the key that signs it, and a public key can't produce a signature anyway.
Incorrect. Only Renee holds her private key, so the CA never has it. A certificate is a third-party attestation, which means the issuer signs it, not the subject.
Incorrect. The CA's public key does the opposite job. Relying parties use it to verify the CA's signature on the certificate, but it can't be used to create that signature.
Correct. The last step in creating a certificate is the digital signature, and the CA makes it with its own private key. Anyone holding the CA's public key can then verify the certificate.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
Mike and Renee would like to use an asymmetric cryptosystem to communicate with each other. They are located in different parts of the country but have exchanged encryption keys by using digital certificates signed by a mutually trusted certificate authority.

When Mike receives Renee's digital certificate, what key does he use to verify the authenticity of the certificate?
questions.explanation: When an individual receives a copy of a digital certificate, the person verifies the authenticity of that certificate by using the CA's public key to validate the digital signature contained on the certificate.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Renee's public key is what the certificate contains and vouches for. It can't be used to check the CA's signature on the certificate, because Renee didn't create that signature.
Incorrect. Renee's private key is known only to Renee, so Mike never has it. In any case, the signature on a certificate is checked with the signer's public key, not with anyone's private key.

Correct. The CA signed the certificate with its private key, so Mike checks that digital signature with the CA's public key. A valid signature shows the certificate is authentic and hasn't been tampered with.
Incorrect. The CA uses its private key to sign certificates, and only the CA holds it. Mike couldn't use it, and verifying a signature needs the matching public key anyway.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
Mike and Renee would like to use an asymmetric cryptosystem to communicate with each other. They are located in different parts of the country but have exchanged encryption keys by using digital certificates signed by a mutually trusted certificate authority.

Mike would like to send Renee a private message using the information gained during this exchange. What key should he use to encrypt the message?
questions.explanation: Mike uses the public key that he extracted from Renee's digital certificate to encrypt the message that he would like to send to Renee.
optionNotes: Correct. Mike takes Renee's public key from her CA-signed certificate and encrypts with it, so only Renee's matching private key can decrypt the message. That keeps it confidential.
Incorrect. Only Renee holds her private key, and she uses it to decrypt. Mike never has access to it, so he can't encrypt with it.
Incorrect. The CA's public key is used to check the signature on Renee's certificate. It doesn't encrypt messages meant for Renee, and she couldn't decrypt anything encrypted with it.
Incorrect. The CA's private key signs certificates and stays secret with the CA. Mike doesn't have it, and it plays no part in encrypting messages between users.

questions.stem: Which one of the following tools may be used to directly violate the confidentiality of communications on an unencrypted VoIP network?
questions.explanation: Wireshark is a network monitoring tool that can capture and replay communications sent over a data network, including Voice over IP (VoIP) communications. Nmap, Nessus, and Nikto are all security tools that may identify security flaws in the network, but they do not directly undermine confidentiality because they do not have the ability to capture communications.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Nmap is a port scanner. It finds open ports and services, but it can't capture VoIP traffic, so it doesn't directly break confidentiality.
Incorrect. Nessus is a vulnerability scanner. It reports security flaws but doesn't capture communications, so it can't directly expose VoIP conversations.
Correct. Wireshark is a packet capture and network monitoring tool. It can record and replay unencrypted VoIP calls, which directly violates their confidentiality.
Incorrect. Nikto is a web server vulnerability scanner. It finds web application flaws but can't capture network communications such as VoIP traffic.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true about the ISC2 Code of Ethics?
options: Adherence to the code is a condition of certification.
Failure to comply with the code may result in revocation of certification.
The code applies to all members of the information security profession.
Members who observe a breach of the code are required to report the possible violation.
questions.explanation: The ISC2 Code of Ethics applies only to information security professionals who are members of ISC2. Adherence to the code is a condition of certification, and individuals found in violation of the code may have their certifications revoked. ISC2 members who observe a breach of the code are required to report the possible violation by following the ethics complaint procedures.
optionNotes: Incorrect. This statement is true, so it isn't the answer. ISC2 makes following the code a condition of earning and keeping certification.
Incorrect. This statement is true, so it isn't the answer. ISC2 can revoke the certification of anyone found to have violated the code.
Correct. This is the false statement, so it's the correct choice. The code binds only ISC2 members and certification holders, not everyone who works in information security.
Incorrect. This statement is true, so it isn't the answer. Members who see a possible breach must report it through ISC2's ethics complaint procedures.

questions.stem: Which one of the following cryptographic algorithms supports the goal of nonrepudiation?
questions.explanation: Nonrepudiation is possible only with an asymmetric encryption algorithm. RSA is an asymmetric algorithm. AES, DES, and Blowfish are all symmetric encryption algorithms that do not provide nonrepudiation.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Blowfish is a symmetric block cipher. Both parties share the same key, so you can't prove which one created a message, and it can't provide nonrepudiation.
Incorrect. DES is a symmetric algorithm. Because the secret key is shared, either party could have produced the message, so DES can't provide nonrepudiation.
Incorrect. AES is a strong symmetric cipher, but every key holder has the same key. That means a sender can't be uniquely tied to a message, so AES doesn't give nonrepudiation.
Correct. RSA is an asymmetric algorithm. A signature made with the sender's private key, which only the sender holds, proves who sent the message, and that is nonrepudiation.

questions.stem: Microsoft's STRIDE threat assessment framework uses six categories for threats: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, and Elevation of Privilege. If a penetration tester is able to modify audit logs, what STRIDE categories best describe this issue?
questions.explanation: Modification of audit logs will allow repudiation because the data cannot be trusted, and thus actions can be provably denied. The modification of the logs is also a direct example of tampering. It might initially be tempting to answer elevation of privileges and tampering, as the attacker made changes to files that should be protected, but this is an unknown without more information. Similarly, the attacker may have accessed the files, resulting in information disclosure in addition to tampering, but again, this is not specified in the question. Finally, this did not cause a denial of service, and thus that answer can be ignored.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Changing the logs is tampering. The question never says the tester read or exposed log contents, though, so information disclosure isn't established, and this pair misses repudiation.
Incorrect. It's tempting because protected files were changed. But the question gives no evidence that the tester gained elevated privileges, so only the tampering half is supported.
Incorrect. Repudiation fits, but modifying logs did not make any service unavailable. Denial of service doesn't apply, and this pair leaves out tampering.
Correct. Altering the logs is direct tampering. Once logs can be altered they can't be trusted, so users can deny their actions, which is repudiation.

questions.stem: Carmen is reviewing her organization's web architecture and realizes that the web server is often under heavy load from users in different regions of the world. This load comes at unpredictable times. She would like to find a solution that minimizes the burden on her organization's servers and places content geographically closer to the user to decrease load time. What would be the best solution to Carmen's requirements?
questions.explanation: Content delivery networks (CDNs) place endpoints at geographic locations around the world and then cache customer content at those endpoints. The CDN servers then handle user requests for data, greatly reducing the burden on the organization's own servers and improving load time. Load balancers would distribute the load among Carmen's own servers and would, therefore, not meet her requirements. TLS acceleration may improve load time by reducing the burden of encryption on servers, but they would not place content closer to end users. Web application firewalls would be used to protect the servers against attack, but this does not match Carmen's requirements.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A load balancer only spreads traffic across Carmen's own servers. Her infrastructure still carries the load, and content sits no closer to users in other regions.
Correct. A CDN caches content at endpoints around the world and answers user requests from those endpoints. This takes load off the organization's servers and cuts load time for distant users.
Incorrect. TLS acceleration offloads encryption work, which can speed up responses. It does not move content geographically closer to end users.
Incorrect. A web application firewall protects web servers from application-layer attacks. It does nothing to reduce load or bring content closer to users.

questions.stem: Brian recently joined an organization that runs the majority of its services on a virtualization platform located in its own data center but also leverages an IaaS provider for hosting its web services and an SaaS email system. What term best describes the type of cloud environment this organization uses?
questions.explanation: The scenario describes a mix of public cloud and private cloud services. This is an example of a hybrid cloud environment.
optionNotes: Incorrect. The IaaS web hosting and SaaS email are public cloud services. Most workloads, though, run on the organization's own virtualization platform, so calling the whole environment public cloud leaves out the private part.

Incorrect. "Dedicated cloud" isn't one of the standard deployment models (public, private, community, hybrid). Nothing in the scenario points to infrastructure dedicated to a single tenant at a provider.

Incorrect. The on-premises virtualization platform counts as a private cloud. However, the organization also uses public IaaS and SaaS services, so private cloud describes only part of its environment.

Correct. The organization combines a private cloud (its own data-center virtualization) with public cloud services (IaaS web hosting and SaaS email). Mixing private and public cloud is the definition of a hybrid cloud.

questions.stem: The government agency that Ben works at installed a new access control system. The system uses information such as Ben's identity, department, normal working hours, job category, and location to make authorization decisions. What type of access control system did Ben's employer adopt?
questions.explanation: Each of the attributes linked to Ben's access provides information for an attribute-based information control system. Attribute-based information controls like those described in NIST SP 800-162 can take many details about the user, actions, and objects into consideration before allowing access to occur. A role-based access control would simply consider Ben's role, whereas both administrative and system discretionary access controls are not commonly used terms to describe access controls.
optionNotes: Incorrect. RBAC would base the decision only on Ben's role or job function. It would not also weigh his location, working hours and department together.
Correct. ABAC (NIST SP 800-162) looks at many attributes of the user, the action and the object, such as identity, department, hours, job category and location, before granting access.
Incorrect. 'Administrative' describes a category of control (policies and procedures), not an access control model. It isn't a standard name for a system that makes authorization decisions.
Incorrect. 'System discretionary access control' isn't a standard term. DAC lets owners decide who gets access and doesn't evaluate a set of attributes.

questions.stem: Ben is building his organization's security awareness and training program and would like to include interactive activities that better engage users. What techniques would best help him meet this goal? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: All of these techniques are valid components of a security awareness and training program. However, users generally find policy reviews and classroom training boring. Gamification and phishing simulations are designed to bring interactivity to the effort and make it more interesting and engaging for users.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Policy reviews are a valid awareness component, but they are passive reading exercises that users generally find boring, not interactive engagement.
Correct. Gamification adds competition, points, and challenges that bring interactivity and make training more interesting and engaging for users.
Incorrect. Classroom training is legitimate but largely lecture-based. Users often find it boring, so it does not meet Ben's goal of interactive engagement.
Correct. Phishing simulations have users respond to realistic test emails. This hands-on interactivity makes the program more engaging.
